title: Black people as psychologists under pressure
summary: Oppressed people learn ruses like the coyote or fox, and Black people raised in Europe do not know their enemy, as with one of Butler's sons.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: So did you say (that you seeible) a lot of the guys throughout that period, you see them more as psychologists or manipulators than --

Yeah. You had to be. You see, any people under pressure, when he comes in this world, well, he knows that this man wants to do something to him. So his mind is adopted to ruses and everything to keep him from doing something to him. So that's a built-in thing. That is why, you test the coyote and the fox. The coyote, he rules you, see, he knows what to do. Because he's been forced to do that. So that's you're forced to do it.

When you catch a man of color being born in Europe, he don't know his enemy. Just like one of my sons, he don't know his enemy. Probably think all these people love him. And he don't know they will chew him up. So, I say, son, be careful a little too much there. there, now. He's loving you / Later on here he comes. Do you know (I don't want to hear it.
